newsitem.title: BELARUS: McDonald's ready for business in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's ready for business in Belarus.

text.p: Belarus, struggling for foreign investment, on Monday became the 100th country to host McDonald's Corp restaurants.

The opening of three fast-food restaurants in Minsk was a big success for McDonald's, Karen Bishop, head of the fast food giant's Belarus branch, told a news conference before Tuesday's official opening for business.
"We have added 10 million potential new daily visitors to our 98 million daily visitors worldwide," she said.
Bishop said McDonald's had invested $6 million in Belarus, bringing foreign investment in the former Soviet republic between Russia and Poland to $19 million this year.
"McDonald's is a kind of indicator of western investments," Igor Butomo, a senior foreign economic relations ministry official, told Reuters.
"This event is very important for us especially since investment now stands at just $19 million."
Three restaurants were opening in Minsk overnight, and another four were planned for other regional centres by 1998.
Last August, residents protested near the site where one restaurant was being built, saying it would attract only rich consumers.
But McDonald's says it hopes to pull in a wide clientele and that it has kept prices low, charging the equivalent of $1 for a "Big Mac" in a country where the average monthly wage is about $50.
Under the rule of hardline President Alexander Lukashenko, who expresses nostalgia for the Soviet past, reforms have slowed and privatisation has ground to a virtual halt.

Lukashenko seized sweeping powers -- attracting criticism from opponents at home and in the West -- after a landslide victory in a referendum last month which the Council of Europe said fell short of minimum democratic standards.
